King Asa also removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her horrid image, crushed it and burned it at the Kidron Valley.
But the high places were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was whole all his days.
He brought into the house of God the things his father had dedicated and the things he himself had dedicated, silver and gold and vessels.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

chapters.title: Asa Relies on Aram
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 16

The Treaty with Ben-hadad

1In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

2Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

3"Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. I am sending you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."

4Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the store cities of Naphtali.

5And it came to pass, when Baasha heard of it, that he stopped building Ramah and let his work cease.

6Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.

Hanani the Seer

7At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.

8Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a huge army, with chariots and horsemen in great number? Yet because you relied on the LORD, He gave them into your hand.

9For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth, to show Himself strong for those whose heart is whole toward Him. You have acted foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars."

10Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks, for he was in a rage with him over this. At that time Asa also crushed some of the people.

The Death of Asa

11The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

12In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was diseased in his feet, and his disease became severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but the healers.

13Asa lay down with his fathers, dying in the forty-first year of his reign.

14They buried him in his own tomb, which he had cut for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and various kinds of ointment prepared by the perfumer's art, and they made a very great fire in his honor.

Notes

  • vv1–6 and 1 Kings 15:17–22 — the same account. Chronicles dates it to the thirty-sixth year of Asa; Kings has Baasha's son Elah reigning already in the twenty-sixth year of Asa (1 Kings 16:8). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v7 "Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD" — be-hisha'enkha… ve-lo nish'anta, the word of Asa's own prayer at Mareshah, we rely on You (14:11). Not in Kings, which tells the treaty without a word of judgment.

  • v8 "the Cushites and the Libyans" — Zerah's army of 14:9–15. Because you relied on the LORD, He gave them into your hand: the seer holds up Asa's own victory against him.

  • v9 "the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth" — einei YHWH meshotetot be-khol ha-arets, the words of Zechariah 4:10, the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth. Whole toward Him, shalem, the word said of Asa's heart in 15:17.

  • v9 "You have acted foolishly" — niskalta, Samuel's word to Saul, You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God (1 Samuel 13:13).

  • v10 "put him in the stocks" — beit ha-mahpekhet, the word of Jeremiah 20:2, where Pashhur put him in the stocks that were in the upper Benjamin Gate. A king of David's line does to a seer what a priest later does to a prophet.

  • v12 "he did not seek the LORD, but the healers" — lo darash et YHWH ki ba-rof'im. The king whose reign was built on seeking the LORD (14:4, 7; 15:2, 12) ends by seeking elsewhere, though the LORD named Himself your healer, rof'ekha (Exodus 15:26).

  • v14 "a very great fire in his honor" — serefah, a burning made for a king at his burial, as Jeremiah promises Zedekiah, as they burned for your fathers, the former kings… so they will burn for you (Jeremiah 34:5). Jehoram is denied it: his people made no fire for him like the fire for his fathers (21:19).

chapters.title: Jehoshaphat Teaches Judah
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 17

Jehoshaphat Strengthened

1Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place and strengthened himself against Israel.

2He placed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had taken.

3The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of David his father and did not seek the Baals,

4but sought the God of his father and walked in His commandments, and not as Israel did.

5So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had riches and honor in abundance.

6His heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD, and he again removed the high places and the Asherim from Judah.

Teachers in the Cities

7In the third year of his reign he sent his officials, Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.

8With them were the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-adonijah, the Levites, and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

9They taught in Judah, having the book of the instruction of the LORD with them. They went around through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.

Tribute and Troops

10The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

11Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabians also brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred goats.

12Jehoshaphat grew steadily greater. He built fortresses and store cities in Judah,

13and he had much work in the cities of Judah, and soldiers, mighty men of valor, in Jerusalem.

14This was their muster by their fathers' houses. Of Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor;

15next to him Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;

16and next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who offered himself willingly to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.

17Of Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;

18and next to him Jehozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand equipped for war.

19These were the men who served the king, besides those the king had placed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

Notes

  • vv1–19 — not in Kings, which gives Jehoshaphat's reign a summary of ten verses (1 Kings 22:41–50) and tells him mostly beside Ahab.

  • v3 "the earlier ways of David his father" — darkhei David aviv ha-rishonim. The Greek has the ways of his father, the earlier ones, without David, and then the father is Asa, whose earlier years were faithful and his last were not (16:7–12). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v6 "His heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD" — va-yigbah libbo. Everywhere else in the book the phrase is pride: Uzziah's heart was lifted up, to his destruction (26:16), and Hezekiah's (32:25). Here alone it is good: his heart was raised high in the LORD's ways.

  • v6 "he again removed the high places" — 20:33 says the high places were not removed, as Kings does (1 Kings 22:43). The text keeps both.

  • vv7–9 "having the book of the instruction of the LORD with them" — sefer torat YHWH, carried from town to town by officials, Levites and priests together. The blessing of Levi: They teach Your rules to Jacob (Deuteronomy 33:10). The same phrase names the book found in Josiah's day (34:14).

  • v10 "The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms" — pachad YHWH, as on the cities around Gerar in Asa's war (14:14). Here it comes without a battle.

  • v16 "who offered himself willingly to the LORD" — ha-mitnaddev, the word of Deborah's song, when the people offer themselves willingly (Judges 5:2, 9), and of the gifts for the house (1 Chronicles 29:5–9).

chapters.title: Micaiah and the Death of Ahab
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 18

The Alliance with Ahab

1Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.

2After some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and oxen in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and he enticed him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.

3Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" He said to him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will be with you in the battle."

4But Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Inquire first for the word of the LORD."

5Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?" They said, "Go up, for God will give it into the hand of the king."

Micaiah Son of Imlah

6But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not here another prophet of the LORD, of whom we may inquire?"

7The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "Let not the king say so."

8Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imla quickly."

9The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, dressed in their robes; they were sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says the LORD: 'With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are destroyed.'"

11All the prophets prophesied so, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper; the LORD will give it into the hand of the king."

12The messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him, "The words of the prophets with one mouth are good for the king. Let your word be like one of theirs, and speak good."

13But Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, what my God says, that I will speak."

14When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micah, shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?" He said, "Go up and prosper; they will be given into your hand."

15But the king said to him, "How many times shall I make you swear that you speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"

16So he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. Then the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his home in peace.'"

17The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"

18Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right hand and on His left.

19The LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One said one thing, and another said another.

20Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' The LORD said to him, 'By what means?'

21He said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' He said, 'You shall entice him, and you shall succeed. Go out and do so.'

22So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these your prophets, and the LORD has spoken evil concerning you."

23Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?"

24Micaiah said, "You shall see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide yourself."

25The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and bring him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,

26and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this man in prison, and feed him with a scant ration of bread and water until I return in peace.'"

27Micaiah said, "If you return in peace at all, the LORD has not spoken by me." Then he said, "Hear, all you peoples!"

The Battle at Ramoth-gilead

28So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

29The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.

30Now the king of Aram had commanded the captains of his chariots, "Fight with neither small nor great, but only with the king of Israel."

31And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "It is the king of Israel." So they turned to fight against him, and Jehoshaphat cried out. The LORD helped him, and God drew them away from him.

32And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.

33But a certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So he said to the driver of his chariot, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the battle, for I am wounded."

34The battle grew hot that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. He died as the sun went down.

Notes

  • vv1–34 and 1 Kings 22:1–35 — the same account; the English follows 1 Kings where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles tells it as part of Jehoshaphat's story and ends with Ahab's death, without the dogs and his burial (1 Kings 22:36–40).

  • vv1–2 "he made a marriage alliance with Ahab… and he enticed him" — va-yitchatten, the marriage of Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram to Ahab's daughter (21:6). Va-yesitehu, enticed him, is the verb of 1 Chronicles 21:1, where Satan incited David. The feast at Samaria is how Jehoshaphat is drawn in. Not in Kings.

  • v10 "horns of iron… With these you shall gore the Arameans" — the picture of Moses' blessing on Joseph, With them he gores the peoples (Deuteronomy 33:17), acted out.

  • v16 "like sheep that have no shepherd" — Moses' words when he asked for a leader (Numbers 27:17). The king dies at sunset (v34).

  • vv18–22 "a spirit came forward… a lying spirit" — ha-ruach, the spirit, one of the host of v18, not the Spirit of the LORD; lowercase, as in 1 Kings 22:21. Zedekiah answers with the Spirit of the LORD (v23).

  • v27 "Hear, all you peoples!" — shim'u ammim kullam, the first words of the book of Micah (Micah 1:2), whose name is a short form of Micaiah. The king calls him Micah in v14.

  • v31 "The LORD helped him, and God drew them away from him" — not in Kings, where Jehoshaphat cried out and the captains simply see their mistake (1 Kings 22:32–33). Va-yesitem, drew them away, is the verb of v2: Ahab enticed Jehoshaphat into the battle, and God enticed the enemy away from him.

  • v34 "propped himself up… until evening. He died as the sun went down" — Kings has the blood of the wound ran into the bottom of the chariot (1 Kings 22:35); Chronicles leaves it out.

chapters.title: Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 19

Jehu Son of Hanani

1Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned in peace to his house in Jerusalem.

2Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath has gone out against you from the LORD.

3Yet good things are found in you, for you have removed the Asherahs from the land and have set your heart to seek God."

Judges in the Land

4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

5He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.

6He said to the judges, "Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for the LORD, and He is with you when you give judgment.

7Now let the fear of the LORD be on you. Take care what you do, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice, no partiality and no taking of bribes."

The Court in Jerusalem

8In Jerusalem also Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and the priests and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, to give judgment for the LORD and to decide disputes. They lived in Jerusalem.

9He charged them, saying, "This is how you shall act: in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and with a whole heart.

10Whenever a case comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities, between blood and blood, between instruction and commandment, statutes and rules, you shall warn them, so that they do not incur guilt before the LORD and wrath come on you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not incur guilt.

11Amariah the chief priest is over you in every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, in every matter of the king. The Levites will serve you as officials. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with the good."

  • vv1–11 — not in Kings. The king's name, Yehoshafat, is the LORD judges, from shafat, the verb of this chapter: judges, shoftim (v5), you do not judge (v6).

  • v2 "Jehu son of Hanani the seer" — the son of the seer Asa put in the stocks for rebuking him (16:7–10). Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD?: the alliance with Ahab of chapter 18.

  • v3 "good things are found in you" — devarim tovim, the words said of Judah under Rehoboam (12:12). The wrath of v2 is not withdrawn; it is set beside them.

  • v4 "from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim" — the old saying for the whole land is from Dan to Beersheba; the kingdom of Judah now reaches only to Ephraim.

  • vv5–7 "judges… in all the fortified cities… no injustice, no partiality and no taking of bribes" — the law of Deuteronomy: Judges and officials you shall appoint for yourself in all your towns (Deuteronomy 16:18); the judgment is God's (1:17); the LORD shows no partiality and takes no bribe (10:17).

  • vv8–10 "between blood and blood" — bein dam le-dam, the words of the law of the central court: If a case is too hard for you in judgment — between blood and blood, between claim and claim… then you shall… go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose (Deuteronomy 17:8). Jehoshaphat sets up that court in Jerusalem.

  • v11 "in every matter of the LORD… in every matter of the king" — the division David made beyond the Jordan, for every matter of God and every matter of the king (1 Chronicles 26:32): a priest over the one, a leader of Judah over the other.

chapters.title: The Battle Is God's
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 20

The Army from Beyond the Sea

1And it came to pass after this that the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.

2Men came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram. They are already in Hazazon-tamar," that is, En-gedi.

3Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set his face to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.

4Judah gathered to seek help from the LORD; from all the cities of Judah they came to seek the LORD.

Jehoshaphat's Prayer

5Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,

6and said, "O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. In Your hand are power and might, so that none can stand against You.

7Did You not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel, and give it forever to the seed of Abraham Your friend?

8They have lived in it and have built You a sanctuary in it for Your name, saying,

9'If evil comes on us, the sword of judgment, or plague, or famine, we will stand before this house and before You, for Your name is in this house, and cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear and save.'

10And now the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom You would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, so that they turned aside from them and did not destroy them —

11they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of Your possession, which You gave us to possess.

12Our God, will You not judge them? For we have no power against this great multitude that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on You."

13All Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives and their sons.

Jahaziel's Word

14Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly.

15He said, "Listen, all Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat. Thus says the LORD to you: Do not be afraid and do not lose heart because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God's.

16Tomorrow go down against them. They will be coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, east of the wilderness of Jeruel.

17You will not need to fight in this battle. Take your positions, stand still and see the deliverance of the LORD with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid and do not lose heart. Tomorrow go out against them, and the LORD will be with you."

18Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD, worshiping the LORD.

19The Levites, of the sons of the Kohathites and of the sons of the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

The Valley of Blessing

20They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in the LORD your God, and you will be established; believe His prophets, and you will succeed."

21When he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed singers to the LORD to praise Him in holy splendor as they went out before the army, saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for His loyal love endures forever."

22When they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the sons of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were struck down.

23The sons of Ammon and Moab rose against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction and wipe them out, and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped to destroy one another.

24When Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, they looked toward the multitude: they were dead bodies lying on the ground, and none had escaped.

25When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their spoil, they found among them goods in abundance, corpses and precious things, more than they could carry away. They were three days taking the spoil, it was so much.

26On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD. That is why the name of that place is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.

27Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returned to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.

28They came to Jerusalem, to the house of the LORD, with harps, lyres and trumpets.

29The fear of God fell on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.

30So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, for his God gave him rest on every side.

The End of Jehoshaphat's Reign

31So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

32He walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

33Yet the high places were not removed; the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their fathers.

34The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which are entered in the book of the kings of Israel.

35After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.

36He joined with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships in Ezion-geber.

37Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have joined with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken down your works." The ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.

Notes

  • v1 "some of the Meunites" — the Hebrew has me-ha-Ammonim, some of the Ammonites, after the sons of Ammon in the same sentence. The Greek has ek tōn Meinaiōn, of the Meunites, a people named again in Uzziah's wars (26:7), and the army is called Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir in vv10, 22–23. The text follows the Greek.

  • v2 "from Aram" — me-Aram, and the Greek agrees, from Syria. Edom, which differs by one letter, would fit an army that includes Mount Seir; no witness here has it. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v7 "the seed of Abraham Your friend" — ohavkha, who loved You, as the LORD calls him in Isaiah 41:8, the seed of Abraham, My friend. James takes it up: he was called the friend of God (James 2:23).

  • v9 "If evil comes on us… You will hear and save" — Solomon's prayer at the dedication (6:28–30), now prayed back.

  • v10 "whom You would not let Israel invade" — the LORD's word in the wilderness: I will not give you any of their land… because I have given Mount Seir to Esau (Deuteronomy 2:5), and the same for Moab and Ammon (2:9, 19).

  • vv15, 17 "the battle is not yours but God's… stand still and see the deliverance of the LORD" — David's words to Goliath, the battle is the LORD's (1 Samuel 17:47), and Moses' at the sea, Stand still and see the deliverance of the LORD (Exodus 14:13).

  • v20 "Believe… and you will be established" — ha'aminu… ve-te'amenu, the same verb twice: trust, and be made firm. Isaiah said it to Ahaz in the negative, If you will not believe, you will not be established (Isaiah 7:9).

  • v26 "the Valley of Beracah" — berakhah, blessing, named for what they did there: there they blessed the LORD.

  • vv35–37 "joined with Ahaziah… the ships were wrecked" — Kings: the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber, and afterward Jehoshaphat would not let Ahaziah's men sail with his (1 Kings 22:48–49). Chronicles has the alliance come first and a prophet name it as the cause.

chapters.title: Jehoram and Elijah's Letter
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 21

Jehoram Kills His Brothers

1Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

2He had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

3Their father gave them great gifts of silver, gold and precious things, with fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.

4When Jehoram had risen over his father's kingdom and established himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the officials of Israel as well.

5Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

6He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

7Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant He had made with David, and since He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.

Edom and Libnah Revolt

8In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and set up a king of their own.

9Then Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots with him. He rose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots.

10So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah to this day. Libnah revolted from under his hand at the same time, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers.

11He also made high places in the hill country of Judah, and led the inhabitants of Jerusalem to whore, and drove Judah astray.

The Letter from Elijah

12A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, "Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

13but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to whore, as the house of Ahab led Israel to whore, and have also killed your brothers, your father's house, who were better than you,

14the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives and all your possessions with a great blow.

15You yourself will have a severe sickness, a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the sickness, day after day."

16The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabians who lived beside the Cushites.

17They came up against Judah, broke into it, and carried away all the possessions found in the king's house, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

18After all this the LORD struck him in his bowels with a sickness that could not be healed.

19In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his sickness, and he died in great pain. His people made no fire for him like the fire for his fathers.

20He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed with no one's regret. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

Notes

  • vv5–10 and 2 Kings 8:16–24 — the same account, with Chronicles' additions: the killing of the brothers (vv2–4), the reason for Libnah's revolt (v10), Elijah's letter (vv12–15) and the manner of his death (vv16–20).

  • v2 "Jehoshaphat king of Israel" — the Greek has king of Judah. Chronicles uses Israel for the people faithful to David's house as well (11:3; 12:6). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v7 "because of the covenant He had made with David… a lamp to him and to his sons" — Kings has the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David His servant (2 Kings 8:19). Chronicles names the covenant, and the house of David instead of Judah.

  • vv11, 13 "led the inhabitants of Jerusalem to whore" — va-yizen, the verb of zanah made causative: the king makes the people whore after other gods, as the house of Ahab led Israel to whore.

  • v12 "A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet" — Elijah's only appearance in Chronicles, and the only writing of his anywhere in Scripture. Kings tells of his being taken up in 2 Kings 2, before it tells of Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 8:16).

  • v14 "the LORD is about to strike… with a great blow" — hinneh YHWH nogef maggefah gedolah, hinneh with a participle, rendered is about to.

  • v17 "Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons" — the king called Ahaziah in 22:1. Yeho-achaz and Achaz-yahu are the same two parts, the divine name and achaz, he has grasped, in reverse order.

  • v19 "His people made no fire for him like the fire for his fathers" — the burning made for Asa at his burial, a very great fire (16:14). Jehoram is buried without it, and not in the tombs of the kings (v20).

  • v20 "He departed with no one's regret" — va-yelekh be-lo chemdah, he went without desire: no one wanted him. The Greek has he went without praise.

chapters.title: Ahaziah and Athaliah
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 22

Ahaziah King of Judah

1The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the band of raiders that came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.

2Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.

3He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in doing wickedly.

4He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father's death they were his counselors, to his destruction.

5He also followed their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

6He returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds that they had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

The Death of Ahaziah

7But the downfall of Ahaziah came from God, through his going to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.

8And it came to pass, when Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, that he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who were serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.

9He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria, brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, for they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." So the house of Ahaziah had no one able to hold the kingdom.

Athaliah and Joash

10When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal seed of the house of Judah.

11But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, because she was Ahaziah's sister, hid him from Athaliah, so that she did not put him to death.

12He was with them in the house of God, hidden for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

Notes

  • vv1–6 and 2 Kings 8:24–29; vv10–12 and 2 Kings 11:1–3 — the same accounts; the English follows Kings where the Hebrew is the same.

  • v1 "the band of raiders that came with the Arabians" — the raid of 21:16–17, which left Jehoram only his youngest son.

  • v2 "twenty-two years old" — the Hebrew has forty-two, but his father died at forty (21:20), so the son cannot have been older. Kings has twenty-two (2 Kings 8:26); the Greek of Chronicles has twenty. The text follows Kings.

  • v2 "Athaliah the daughter of Omri" — bat Omri: Omri was Ahab's father, so daughter here means a woman of his house; she is called the daughter of Ahab in 21:6.

  • v6 "Ahaziah son of Jehoram" — the Hebrew has Azariah son of Jehoram, against vv1, 2 and 7. The Greek has Ochozias, Ahaziah, as Kings does (2 Kings 8:29). The text follows the Greek.

  • v7 "the downfall of Ahaziah came from God" — tevusah, a word found only here, from bus, to trample. Kings tells the visit without saying whose hand was in it.

  • v9 "they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria… They buried him" — Kings tells it differently: Ahaziah fled, was struck at the ascent of Gur, fled to Megiddo and died there, and his servants carried him to Jerusalem to be buried with his fathers (2 Kings 9:27–28). In Chronicles Jehu's men bury him, out of respect for his grandfather, who sought the LORD with all his heart. The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v11 "Jehoshabeath… the wife of Jehoiada the priest" — Kings calls her Jehosheba and does not say she was the priest's wife (2 Kings 11:2). Chronicles gives the reason the child could be hidden in the house of God for six years.

Ahaziah King of Judah

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the band of raiders that came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in doing wickedly.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father's death they were his counselors, to his destruction.
He also followed their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

He returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds that they had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

But the downfall of Ahaziah came from God, through his going to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it came to pass, when Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, that he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who were serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.

He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria, brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, for they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." So the house of Ahaziah had no one able to hold the kingdom.

When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal seed of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, because she was Ahaziah's sister, hid him from Athaliah, so that she did not put him to death.
He was with them in the house of God, hidden for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

chapters.title: Jehoiada Makes Joash King
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 23

The Covenant in the House of God

1In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant with the commanders of the hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri.

2They went around through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.

3All the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "The king's son shall reign, as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David.

4This is what you shall do: a third of you, priests and Levites who come on duty on the Sabbath, shall be gatekeepers at the thresholds;

5a third shall be at the king's house, and a third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD.

6Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who minister. They may enter, for they are holy, but all the people shall keep the charge of the LORD.

7The Levites shall surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand, and whoever enters the house shall be put to death. Be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."

8The Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath with those going off duty on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest did not release the divisions.

9Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of the hundreds the spears and the large and small shields that had been King David's, which were in the house of God.

10He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and the house, around the king.

Joash Crowned, Athaliah Killed

11Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown and the testimony on him, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they said, "Long live the king!"

12When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people in the house of the LORD.

13She looked, and there was the king standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with instruments of song leading the praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"

14Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of the hundreds who were set over the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to death with the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."

15So they laid hands on her, and she went into the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's house, and there they put her to death.

The Covenant Renewed

16Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be the LORD's people.

17All the people went to the house of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

18Jehoiada placed the oversight of the house of the LORD in the hands of the Levitical priests whom David had organized over the house of the LORD, to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD, as it is written in the instruction of Moses, with rejoicing and with song, as David had directed.

19He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one unclean in anything should enter.

20He took the commanders of the hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They came through the Upper Gate to the king's house and set the king on the throne of the kingdom.

21All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. They had put Athaliah to death with the sword.

Notes

  • vv1–21 and 2 Kings 11:4–20 — the same account; the English follows Kings where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles names the five commanders (v1), which Kings does not.

  • vv2, 4–8 the Levites — in Kings the guard is the Carites and the guard (2 Kings 11:4, 19), the royal bodyguard, and they stand in the house of the LORD. In Chronicles the Levites take their place and the house is kept for those who may enter it: Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites… for they are holy (v6).

  • v3 "as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David" — the promise of 1 Chronicles 17:11–14. With only one son of David left alive, the covenant is made to keep the promise.

  • v11 "the crown and the testimony" — ha-nezer ve-ha-edut. The testimony is the word for the tablets of the covenant (Exodus 25:16); here something put on the king or given into his hand, perhaps the law of the king, he shall write for himself a copy of this instruction (Deuteronomy 17:18). The Hebrew does not say what it was.

  • v13 "the singers with instruments of song leading the praise" — not in Kings. Chronicles sets the Levite singers in the crowd at the crowning.

  • v16 "a covenant between himself and all the people and the king" — Kings has between the LORD and the king and the people (2 Kings 11:17). Chronicles has the priest himself stand as a party to the covenant.

  • vv18–19 "as it is written in the instruction of Moses… as David had directed… no one unclean" — not in Kings. The order of the house is set back as Moses wrote it and David arranged it, and gatekeepers are posted against the unclean.

chapters.title: Joash Repairs the House and Turns Away
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 24

The Repair of the House

1Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.

2Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

3Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.

4And it came to pass after this that Joash set his heart on restoring the house of the LORD.

5He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and gather money from all Israel to repair the house of your God, year by year, and see that you act on it quickly." But the Levites did not act quickly.

6So the king called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax that Moses the servant of the LORD laid on the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?"

7For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God, and had also used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.

8So the king gave orders, and they made a chest and set it outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.

9A proclamation was made through Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God laid on Israel in the wilderness.

10All the officials and all the people rejoiced, and they brought it and threw it into the chest until it was full.

11Whenever the chest was brought to the king's officers by the hand of the Levites, and they saw that there was much money, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, and take it and return it to its place. So they did day after day, and gathered money in abundance.

12The king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.

13So the workmen worked, and the repair went forward in their hands. They set up the house of God according to its proper design and made it strong.

14When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made vessels for the house of the LORD, vessels for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and vessels of gold and silver. They offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually all the days of Jehoiada.

The Death of Jehoiada

15Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died. He was a hundred and thirty years old at his death.

16They buried him in the City of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, and toward God and His house.

17After the death of Jehoiada the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king, and the king listened to them.

18They forsook the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherim and the idols. Wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.

19Yet He sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. They testified against them, but they would not listen.

Zechariah Son of Jehoiada

20Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "Thus says God: Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you."

21But they conspired against him, and at the command of the king they stoned him with stones in the court of the house of the LORD.

22So Joash the king did not remember the loyal love that Jehoiada, Zechariah's father, had shown him, but killed his son. As he was dying, he said, "May the LORD see and require it!"

The Death of Joash

23And it came to pass at the turn of the year that the army of Aram came up against him. They came to Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people, and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.

24Though the army of Aram had come with few men, the LORD gave a very great army into their hand, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers. So they executed judgment on Joash.

25When they had departed from him, leaving him in great sickness, his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and killed him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the City of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.

26These are the men who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.

27As for his sons, the many oracles against him and the rebuilding of the house of God, they are written in the account of the book of the kings. Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–14, 23–27 and 2 Kings 12 — the same reign. Chronicles adds what happened after Jehoiada died (vv15–22), and makes the Aramean war a judgment (v24). Kings has Hazael come up and Joash buy him off with the holy things (2 Kings 12:17–18).

  • v2 "all the days of Jehoiada the priest" — Kings has all his days, in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him (2 Kings 12:2). Chronicles divides the reign at the priest's death (v17).

  • vv6, 9 "the tax that Moses the servant of the LORD laid on the assembly" — the half-shekel of Exodus 30, the atonement silver… for the service of the tent of meeting (Exodus 30:16). Kings makes the chest the priest's doing and sets it beside the altar (2 Kings 12:9); here the king orders it and it stands outside, at the gate.

  • v16 "They buried him in the City of David among the kings" — the priest is buried with the kings; Joash, the king, is not (v25), nor was Jehoram (21:20).

  • v20 "the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah" — lavshah, the word of Judges 6:34, The Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon. You have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you: Shemaiah's word to Rehoboam (12:5) and Azariah's to Asa (15:2).

  • vv21–22 "they stoned him… in the court of the house of the LORD… May the LORD see and require it!" — Jesus names a Zechariah as the last of the righteous killed, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar (Matthew 23:35). Matthew gives the father as Berechiah, the father of the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1).

  • v24 "with few men… a very great army into their hand" — the reverse of Asa's prayer, there is none besides You to help, between the mighty and those who have no strength (14:11).

  • v25 "because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada" — benei, sons, plural; only Zechariah's death is told. The Greek has son.

  • v26 "Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman" — Kings has Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer (2 Kings 12:21). Chronicles names their mothers, and both foreign.

chapters.title: Amaziah and the Gods of Edom
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 25

Amaziah King of Judah

1Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

2He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart.

3And it came to pass, when the kingdom was firmly his, that he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.

4But he did not put their sons to death, according to what is written in the instruction, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers; each shall die for his own sin."

The Hired Army of Israel

5Amaziah gathered Judah and set them by fathers' houses under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered those twenty years old and upward, and found three hundred thousand chosen men fit for war, able to handle spear and shield.

6He also hired a hundred thousand mighty men of valor from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.

7But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with any of the sons of Ephraim.

8Even if you go and act and are strong for the battle, God will make you fall before the enemy, for God has power to help and to make fall."

9Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what shall we do about the hundred talents I have given to the troops of Israel?" The man of God answered, "The LORD is able to give you much more than this."

10So Amaziah separated the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. Their anger burned greatly against Judah, and they returned home in fierce anger.

11Amaziah took courage and led out his people. He went to the Valley of Salt and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir.

12The sons of Judah took another ten thousand alive, brought them to the top of the rock and threw them down from the top of the rock, and they were all dashed to pieces.

13But the troops whom Amaziah had sent back, so that they did not go with him to battle, raided the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down three thousand of them and took much plunder.

The Gods of Seir

14And it came to pass, after Amaziah came back from striking down the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up as his gods. He bowed down before them and burned incense to them.

15The anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent a prophet to him, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of a people who did not deliver their own people from your hand?"

16And it came to pass, as he was speaking to him, that the king said to him, "Have we made you the king's counselor? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" So the prophet stopped, but said, "I know that God has counseled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."

The War with Joash of Israel

17Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face each other."

18Joash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "A thistle in Lebanon sent to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as wife.' Then a wild beast in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.

19You say, 'I have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay at home. Why should you provoke trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"

20But Amaziah would not listen, for it was from God, so that He might give them into Joash's hand, because they had sought the gods of Edom.

21So Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.

22Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his tent.

23Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh. He brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

24He took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God in the care of Obed-edom, and the treasuries of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.

The Death of Amaziah

25Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

26The rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?

27From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.

28They carried him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.

Notes

  • vv1–4, 11, 17–28 and 2 Kings 14:1–20 — the same reign; the English follows Kings where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles adds the hired army and the man of God (vv5–10, 13) and the gods of Seir (vv14–16), which explain the defeat that Kings tells without a cause.

  • v2 "yet not with a whole heart" — ve-lo be-levav shalem. Kings has yet not like David his father (2 Kings 14:3).

  • v4 "Fathers shall not die for sons" — the law of Deuteronomy 24:16, Fathers shall not be put to death for sons. Kings quotes it the same way (2 Kings 14:6); Chronicles has yamutu, shall die, where Kings and Deuteronomy have yumtu, shall be put to death.

  • v8 "Even if you go and act and are strong for the battle, God will make you fall" — the Hebrew is short and abrupt, for if you go, act, be strong for the battle, God will make you fall. The Greek reads it as a condition, if you think to be strong in these. The text takes it the same way.

  • v12 "brought them to the top of the rock and threw them down" — ha-sela, the rock, also the name of the city Amaziah took in this war, Sela (2 Kings 14:7).

  • vv15–16 "counselor… counseled… my counsel" — ya'ats three times: Have we made you the king's counselor?, God has counseled to destroy you, you have not listened to my counsel. Then Amaziah… took counsel (v17), and goes to war.

  • v20 "for it was from God… because they had sought the gods of Edom" — not in Kings. The king who asked Why should you be struck down? (v16) is struck down. From God, as Ahaziah's downfall was (22:7) and Rehoboam's folly (10:15).

  • v24 "in the care of Obed-edom" — the family set over the storehouse of the house (1 Chronicles 26:15).

Amaziah King of Judah
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart.
And it came to pass, when the kingdom was firmly his, that he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he did not put their sons to death, according to what is written in the instruction, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers; each shall die for his own sin."
The Hired Army of Israel

Amaziah gathered Judah and set them by fathers' houses under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered those twenty years old and upward, and found three hundred thousand chosen men fit for war, able to handle spear and shield.
He also hired a hundred thousand mighty men of valor from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with any of the sons of Ephraim.
Even if you go and act and are strong for the battle, God will make you fall before the enemy, for God has power to help and to make fall."
Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what shall we do about the hundred talents I have given to the troops of Israel?" The man of God answered, "The LORD is able to give you much more than this."
So Amaziah separated the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. Their anger burned greatly against Judah, and they returned home in fierce anger.
Amaziah took courage and led out his people. He went to the Valley of Salt and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir.
The sons of Judah took another ten thousand alive, brought them to the top of the rock and threw them down from the top of the rock, and they were all dashed to pieces.

But the troops whom Amaziah had sent back, so that they did not go with him to battle, raided the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down three thousand of them and took much plunder.
The Gods of Seir

And it came to pass, after Amaziah came back from striking down the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up as his gods. He bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
The anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent a prophet to him, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of a people who did not deliver their own people from your hand?"

And it came to pass, as he was speaking to him, that the king said to him, "Have we made you the king's counselor? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" So the prophet stopped, but said, "I know that God has counseled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
The War with Joash of Israel
Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face each other."

Joash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "A thistle in Lebanon sent to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as wife.' Then a wild beast in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You say, 'I have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay at home. Why should you provoke trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen, for it was from God, so that He might give them into Joash's hand, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his tent.

Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh. He brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
He took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God in the care of Obed-edom, and the treasuries of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.
The Death of Amaziah
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
They carried him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.

chapters.title: Uzziah's Strength and His Blight
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 26

Uzziah King of Judah

1All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

2He built Eloth and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his fathers.

3Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

4He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

5He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.

His Wars and His Works

6He went out and made war against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod. He built cities in the region of Ashdod and among the Philistines.

7God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabians who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.

8The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.

9Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and fortified them.

10He built towers in the wilderness and cut out many cisterns, for he had much livestock, in the lowland and in the plain, and farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.

11Uzziah had an army of fighting men who went out to war by divisions, by the number of their muster made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.

12The whole number of the heads of fathers' houses, mighty men of valor, was two thousand six hundred.

13Under their hand was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, who made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.

14Uzziah prepared for all the army shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows and stones for slinging.

15In Jerusalem he made engines, devised by skillful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones. His fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped, until he was strong.

Uzziah in the House of the LORD

16But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, to his destruction. He broke faith with the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.

17Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of courage.

18They stood against King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have broken faith, and it will bring you no honor from the LORD God."

19Uzziah was angry. He had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he was angry with the priests, blight broke out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.

20Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned toward him, and there he was with blight on his forehead. They hurried him out of there, and he himself hastened to go out, because the LORD had struck him.

21King Uzziah had blight until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, having blight, for he was cut off from the house of the LORD. Jotham his son was over the king's house, governing the people of the land.

22The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote.

23Uzziah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He has blight." Jotham his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–4, 21–23 and 2 Kings 14:21–22; 15:1–7 — Kings calls him Azariah and gives him seven verses: he did right, the LORD struck the king, and he had blight (2 Kings 15:5), and he died. Chronicles tells why he was struck (vv16–20).

  • v5 "who had understanding in the visions of God" — ha-mevin bi-r'ot ha-Elohim, in the seeing of God. The Greek has in the fear of the Lord, which is be-yir'at in Hebrew, the same letters with one more. The text keeps the Hebrew. As long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper: the condition of the whole reign, set before it is told.

  • v10 "for he loved the soil" — ki ohev adamah hayah, he was a lover of the ground, the only king of whom it is said. Noah began as a man of the ground (Genesis 9:20).

  • vv15–16 "he was marvelously helped, until he was strong. But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up" — ad ki chazaq… u-khe-chezqato, the same word end to start: the help that made him strong is what lifted him up. His heart was lifted up is said in the good sense of Jehoshaphat alone (17:6); here it is pride, to his destruction.

  • vv16–18 "to burn incense on the altar of incense… It is not for you" — the law after Korah's rebellion: no outsider, who is not of the offspring of Aaron, should come near to burn incense before the LORD, and become like Korah and his company (Numbers 16:40).

  • v19 "blight broke out on his forehead" — tsara'at, blight. Zarechah, broke out, is the word for the sun rising. The forehead is where the high priest wore the gold plate engraved Holy to the LORD: It shall be on Aaron's forehead… always (Exodus 28:36–38).

  • v21 "He lived in a separate house… cut off from the house of the LORD" — beit ha-chofshit, written ha-chofshut, the phrase of 2 Kings 15:5, found only in these two places. The man who forced his way into the house is shut out of it for life.

  • v22 "Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote" — Isaiah's book is dated in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah (Isaiah 1:1), and his call came in the year that King Uzziah died (Isaiah 6:1).

chapters.title: Jotham
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 27

1Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.

2He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Uzziah his father had done, except that he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still acted corruptly.

3He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and built much on the wall of Ophel.

4He built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded hills he built fortresses and towers.

5He fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed against them. The Ammonites gave him that year a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same in the second year and the third.

6So Jotham became strong, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.

7The rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and his ways, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

8He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

9Jotham lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–3, 7–9 and 2 Kings 15:32–38 — the same reign. Chronicles leaves out Kings' last word on it, the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah (2 Kings 15:37), and gives the Ammonite war instead (v5).

  • v2 "except that he did not enter the temple of the LORD" — raq lo va el heikhal YHWH: he did all his father did, except the thing that brought his father's blight (26:16–21). But the people still acted corruptly: Kings has the high places were not taken away (2 Kings 15:35).

  • v6 "So Jotham became strong, because he ordered his ways before the LORD" — va-yitchazzeq, the word of Uzziah's rise and fall: he was marvelously helped, until he was strong. But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up (26:15–16). Jotham's strength has a reason, and the chapter ends before it can turn.

  • v8 "He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign" — the words of v1 again. The Greek does not repeat them.

chapters.title: Ahaz and the Captives of Judah
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 28

Ahaz King of Judah

1Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as David his father had done.

2He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and even made cast images for the Baals.

3He burned incense in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.

4He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills and under every leafy tree.

Defeat by Aram and Israel

5So the LORD his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram, who struck him and carried away a great number of captives and brought them to Damascus. He was also given into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him with a great slaughter.

6Pekah son of Remaliah killed a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day, all of them men of valor, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers.

7Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the governor of the house and Elkanah, who was second to the king.

8The sons of Israel took captive from their kinsmen two hundred thousand women, sons and daughters, and also took much spoil from them and brought the spoil to Samaria.

Oded and the Leaders of Ephraim

9A prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded. He went out to meet the army that was coming to Samaria and said to them, "Because the LORD, the God of your fathers, was angry with Judah, He gave them into your hand; but you have killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven.

10Now you intend to subjugate the sons of Judah and Jerusalem as your male and female slaves. But are there not guilty deeds of your own against the LORD your God?

11So now hear me, and send back the captives you have taken from your kinsmen, for the burning anger of the LORD is on you."

12Then some of the heads of the sons of Ephraim, Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai, stood up against those who were coming from the war,

13and said to them, "You shall not bring the captives in here, for you intend to bring on us guilt against the LORD in addition to our sins and our guilt. Our guilt is already great, and there is burning anger against Israel."

14So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the officials and all the assembly.

15The men who had been named rose up and took the captives. From the spoil they clothed all who were naked among them. They clothed them, gave them sandals, fed them and gave them drink, and anointed them; they carried all the feeble on donkeys and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their kinsmen. Then they returned to Samaria.

Ahaz Seeks Help from Assyria

16At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.

17The Edomites had come again and struck Judah and carried away captives,

18and the Philistines had raided the cities of the lowland and the Negev of Judah, and had taken Beth-shemesh, Aijalon and Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages and Gimzo with its villages, and they lived there.

19For the LORD brought Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let Judah loose and had broken faith with the LORD.

20Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and distressed him, and did not strengthen him.

21For Ahaz took a portion from the house of the LORD, from the house of the king and from the officials, and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.

22In the time of his distress he broke faith with the LORD still more. This was King Ahaz.

23He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, which had struck him, and said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will sacrifice to them, so that they may help me." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.

24Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God and cut the vessels of the house of God in pieces. He shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and he made himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.

25In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked the LORD, the God of his fathers, to anger.

26The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

27Ahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, for they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–4, 16–27 and 2 Kings 16 — the same reign, told with other events. Kings tells of the altar copied from Damascus (2 Kings 16:10–16); Chronicles tells of the war with Israel and the captives (vv5–15), and of Ahaz shutting the doors of the house (v24).

  • v3 "burned his sons in the fire" — va-yav'er et banav ba-esh. Kings has made his son pass through the fire (2 Kings 16:3). Detestable practices, to'avot.

  • vv5–8 "a hundred and twenty thousand… two hundred thousand women, sons and daughters" — not in Kings, which says only that Rezin and Pekah besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him (2 Kings 16:5).

  • v9 "a rage that has reached up to heaven" — be-za'af ad la-shamayim higgia: Israel was the LORD's instrument, and went beyond what it was given to do.

  • vv12–15 "they clothed them… fed them… anointed them… carried all the feeble on donkeys… to Jericho" — men of Samaria, who were not of Judah, take their enemies to Jericho with clothing, food, oil and donkeys. Jesus tells of a man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho who was stripped and left half dead, and of a Samaritan who bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, and set him on his own animal (Luke 10:30–34).

  • vv16, 20–23 "for help… did not strengthen him… it did not help him… so that they may help me" — la'zor, to help, four times: Ahaz seeks help from Assyria and from the gods of Damascus. They were the ruin of him, le-hakhshilo, to make him stumble, the word of 25:8, God has power to help and to make fall.

  • v19 "he had let Judah loose" — hifria, the word of Exodus 32:25, the people… were let loose, for Aaron had let them loose, at the golden calf. Ahaz king of Israel: Chronicles uses Israel for Judah's king, as in 21:2.

  • v24 "He shut the doors of the house of the LORD" — the first act of his son: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD (29:3).

  • v27 "they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings" — Kings says he was buried with his fathers in the City of David (2 Kings 16:20). Chronicles keeps him out, as it kept Jehoram (21:20) and Joash (24:25); Uzziah lay in the burial field that belonged to the kings (26:23).

chapters.title: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the LORD
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 29

The Doors Opened

1Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah the daughter of Zechariah.

2He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that David his father had done.

3In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.

4He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square on the east,

5and said to them, "Hear me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, and carry the filth out of the holy place.

6For our fathers broke faith and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They forsook Him, turned their faces away from the dwelling of the LORD and turned their backs.

8So the wrath of the LORD came on Judah and Jerusalem, and He made them an object of horror, of astonishment and of hissing, as you see with your own eyes.

10Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that His burning anger may turn away from us.

The Cleansing

12Then the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; of the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;

13of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;

14of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
