21They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary and for Judah. He told the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD.

22So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and dashed it against the altar. They slaughtered the rams and dashed the blood against the altar. They slaughtered the lambs and dashed the blood against the altar.

32The number of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to the LORD.

33The consecrated offerings were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.

  • v3 "In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors" — the doors his father had shut (28:24). The first month is the month of Passover, which comes in the next chapter.

  • v5 "carry the filth out of the holy place" — ha-niddah, the word of the law of a woman's monthly separation, she shall be in her monthly separation seven days (Leviticus 15:19). Hezekiah uses the strongest word of uncleanness for what is in the house.

  • v6 "turned their faces away… and turned their backs" — va-yittenu oref, gave the back of the neck: the posture of a people who will not look.

  • v8 "an object of horror, of astonishment and of hissing" — le-za'avah le-shammah ve-lishreqah, the words of Jeremiah 29:18, written and read the same way there: le-zo'ah, read le-za'avah.

  • vv21, 24 "for the kingdom, for the sanctuary and for Judah… for all Israel" — the king widens the atonement: the king had commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be for all Israel, the north as well. The invitation to the north follows in 30:1.

  • v25 "the command was from the LORD through His prophets" — the order of the singers, given by David with Gad and Nathan (1 Chronicles 25), is counted as the LORD's command.

  • v31 "Now you have consecrated yourselves" — mille'tem yedkhem, you have filled your hand, the words for ordaining a priest (1 Chronicles 29:5), said here to the whole assembly.

  • v34 "the Levites were more upright in heart in consecrating themselves than the priests" — yishrei levav, an open word of praise for the Levites over the priests, in a book that keeps their duties apart.

  • v36 "for the thing had come about suddenly" — ki ve-fit'om hayah ha-davar: sixteen days from the opening of the doors to the end of the offerings (v17).

chapters.title: Hezekiah's Passover
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 30

The Letters to All Israel

1Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the LORD at Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.

2For the king and his officials and all the assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel to keep the Passover in the second month,

3because they could not keep it at its time, since not enough priests had consecrated themselves, and the people had not gathered at Jerusalem.

4The thing seemed right to the king and to all the assembly.

5So they decreed to make a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that they should come to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, at Jerusalem, for they had not kept it in great numbers as it is written.

6So the couriers went with the letters from the king and his officials throughout all Israel and Judah, as the king had commanded, saying, "Sons of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, so that He may return to the remnant of you who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.

7Do not be like your fathers and your brothers, who broke faith with the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that He made them a desolation, as you see.

8Now do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did. Give your hand to the LORD and come to His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, so that His burning anger may turn away from you.

9For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and your sons will find compassion before their captors and return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him."

10So the couriers passed from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun, but they laughed them to scorn and mocked them.

11Yet some men of Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

12In Judah also the hand of God was on them to give them one heart to do the command of the king and the officials by the word of the LORD.

The Feast in the Second Month

13Many people gathered at Jerusalem to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very great assembly.

14They arose and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and they removed all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley.

15They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites were ashamed, and they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.

16They stood at their posts as prescribed, according to the instruction of Moses the man of God. The priests dashed the blood that they received from the hand of the Levites.

17For there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves, so the Levites had charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to consecrate them to the LORD.

18For a majority of the people, many of them from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover otherwise than as it is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the good LORD pardon everyone

19who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his fathers, even though not according to the purity of the sanctuary."

20The LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

21The sons of Israel who were present at Jerusalem kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days with great joy, and the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day by day with loud instruments to the LORD.

22Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good understanding in the service of the LORD. They ate the food of the festival for the seven days, sacrificing peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

23Then the whole assembly took counsel to keep another seven days, and they kept another seven days with joy.

24For Hezekiah king of Judah gave the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for offerings, and the officials gave the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. The priests also consecrated themselves in great numbers.

25All the assembly of Judah rejoiced, with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, and the guests who came from the land of Israel and who lived in Judah.

26So there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had been nothing like it in Jerusalem.

27Then the Levitical priests arose and blessed the people. Their voice was heard, and their prayer came to His holy dwelling in heaven.

Notes

  • vv1–27 — not in Kings, which tells of Josiah's Passover as the first since the judges (2 Kings 23:22). Chronicles gives Hezekiah one as well, and opens it to the north.

  • vv2–3, 15 "to keep the Passover in the second month" — the law allows it for one who is unclean because of a corpse, or is away on a long journey: In the second month, on the fourteenth day… they shall keep it (Numbers 9:10–11). Here the whole people use the provision, for both reasons: the priests were not consecrated, and the people were not gathered.

  • v5 "from Beersheba to Dan" — the whole land, as before the kingdom divided. Jehoshaphat's reform reached from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim (19:4).

  • vv6–9 "return to the LORD… so that He may return… if you return to Him" — shuvu… ve-yashov… u-ve-shuvkhem, the verb shuv five times in four verses: Israel's turning, the LORD's turning, and the captives' return to the land.

  • v8 "do not stiffen your necks… Give your hand to the LORD" — the charge of Exodus, it is a stiff-necked people (Exodus 32:9). Tenu yad, give a hand, is a pledge, the word for Solomon's officials pledging themselves to him (1 Chronicles 29:24).

  • v9 "the LORD your God is gracious and merciful" — chanun ve-rachum, the name proclaimed on Sinai, God merciful and gracious (Exodus 34:6), with the two words in the other order.

  • vv18–20 "May the good LORD pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God… The LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people" — the uncleanness of those who ate is not denied; the king asks that a heart that seeks be counted over it, and the LORD answers. Healed, va-yirpa, the word of the promise at the dedication, I will hear from heaven… and heal their land (7:14).

  • v26 "since the days of Solomon" — since the dedication, when the people also kept the feast and then seven days more (7:8–9).

  • v27 "their prayer came to His holy dwelling in heaven" — Solomon's prayer, Hear from the place of Your dwelling, from the heavens (6:21), answered.

chapters.title: The Heaps of the Offerings
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 31

The High Places Torn Down

1When all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and broke the pillars, cut down the Asherim, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout all Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the sons of Israel returned, every man to his possession, to their cities.

The Portions for the Priests and Levites

2Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to his service, the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks and to praise in the gates of the camp of the LORD.

3The king's portion from his own possessions was for the burnt offerings: the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed feasts, as it is written in the instruction of the LORD.

4He told the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion due to the priests and the Levites, so that they might hold fast to the instruction of the LORD.

5As soon as the word spread, the sons of Israel gave in abundance the first of their grain, new wine, oil, honey and all the produce of the field, and they brought in the tithe of everything in abundance.

6The sons of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of the holy things that were consecrated to the LORD their God, and laid them in heaps.

7In the third month they began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.

8When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and His people Israel.

9Hezekiah inquired of the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

10Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answered him, "Since they began to bring the contributions into the house of the LORD, we have eaten and been satisfied and have plenty left over, for the LORD has blessed His people, and what is left is this great store."

The Overseers

11Then Hezekiah told them to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them.

12They brought in the contributions, the tithes and the consecrated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was the officer in charge of them, and Shimei his brother was second;

13and Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the chief officer of the house of God.

14Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the keeper of the east gate, was over the freewill offerings to God, to give out the contribution of the LORD and the most holy things.

15Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah in the cities of the priests, to give faithfully to their brothers by divisions, to great and small alike,

16apart from those enrolled by genealogy, males from three years old and upward, all who entered the house of the LORD as the duty of each day required, for their service in their charges by their divisions;

17and the priests were enrolled by their fathers' houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their charges by their divisions.

18They were enrolled with all their little ones, their wives, their sons and their daughters, the whole assembly, for they were faithful in keeping themselves holy.

19For the sons of Aaron, the priests, who were in the fields of pasture land of their cities, in every city there were men designated by name to give portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.

20So Hezekiah did throughout all Judah. He did what was good and right and true before the LORD his God.

21In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the instruction and in the commandment, to seek his God, he acted with all his heart, and he prospered.

Notes

  • v1 "broke the pillars, cut down the Asherim, and tore down the high places" — Kings gives Hezekiah this act alone, He removed the high places, broke the pillars and cut down the Asherah (2 Kings 18:4). Here the people do it, in Ephraim and Manasseh as well as Judah.

  • v2 "the gates of the camp of the LORD" — machanot YHWH, the word of the wilderness, where the tent set out… in the middle of the camps (Numbers 2:17). The house in Jerusalem is still spoken of as the camp around the dwelling.

  • vv4–6 "the portion due to the priests and the Levites… the first… the tithe" — the law of Numbers 18: the first of the oil… the new wine and the grain to the priests (18:12), and every tenth in Israel to the Levites in return for the service they do (18:21). So that they might hold fast to the instruction of the LORD: provided for, they are free for it.

  • v7 "In the third month… and in the seventh month they finished" — from the grain harvest to the ingathering of fruit: the Festival of Weeks falls fifty days after Passover, and the Festival of Booths in the seventh month (Leviticus 23:15–16, 34). The heaps grew through the whole harvest.

  • v10 "we have eaten and been satisfied and have plenty left over" — akhol ve-savoa ve-hoter, the words of the promise, You will eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 8:10). Hezekiah and the officials do bless Him (v8).

  • vv12, 15, 18 "faithfully" — be-emunah, three times: the stores were brought in faithfully, given out faithfully, and the priests kept themselves holy in their faithfulness.

  • v16 "males from three years old and upward" — an odd age for those who entered the house of the LORD for service; the Greek has it too. Read with apart from, it may count the boys of the priestly families who received a share. The Hebrew does not say more.

  • vv20–21 "good and right and true… with all his heart, and he prospered" — ha-tov ve-ha-yashar ve-ha-emet. Of Hezekiah alone among the kings does Chronicles say all three.

When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and His people Israel.
Hezekiah inquired of the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answered him, "Since they began to bring the contributions into the house of the LORD, we have eaten and been satisfied and have plenty left over, for the LORD has blessed His people, and what is left is this great store."
The Overseers
Then Hezekiah told them to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them.
They brought in the contributions, the tithes and the consecrated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was the officer in charge of them, and Shimei his brother was second;

and Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the chief officer of the house of God.

Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah in the cities of the priests, to give faithfully to their brothers by divisions, to great and small alike,

They were enrolled with all their little ones, their wives, their sons and their daughters, the whole assembly, for they were faithful in keeping themselves holy.

For the sons of Aaron, the priests, who were in the fields of pasture land of their cities, in every city there were men designated by name to give portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.
So Hezekiah did throughout all Judah. He did what was good and right and true before the LORD his God.
In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the instruction and in the commandment, to seek his God, he acted with all his heart, and he prospered.

chapters.title: Sennacherib's Invasion and Hezekiah's End
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 32

The Defense of Jerusalem

1After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah. He encamped against the fortified cities and thought to break into them for himself.

2When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and meant to make war against Jerusalem,

3he took counsel with his officials and his mighty men to stop the water of the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.

4Many people gathered and stopped all the springs and the brook that flowed through the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?"

5He took courage and built up all the wall that was broken down, and raised towers on it, and built another wall outside it. He strengthened the Millo in the City of David, and made weapons and shields in abundance.

6He set commanders of war over the people, gathered them to him in the square at the gate of the city, and spoke encouragingly to them, saying,

7"Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid and do not lose heart because of the king of Assyria and all the multitude that is with him, for there is more with us than with him.

8With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." The people relied on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

Sennacherib's Taunts

9After this Sennacherib king of Assyria, who was besieging Lachish with all his forces, sent his servants to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,

10"Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: On what are you trusting, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?

11Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by hunger and thirst, when he says, 'The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria'?

12Is it not this same Hezekiah who has removed His high places and His altars, and told Judah and Jerusalem, 'You shall bow down before one altar, and on it you shall burn incense'?

13Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to deliver their land from my hand?

14Who among all the gods of those nations that my fathers devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?

15So now do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you from my hand!"

16His servants said still more against the LORD God and against Hezekiah His servant.

17He also wrote letters to defy the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against Him, saying, "As the gods of the nations of the lands have not delivered their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver His people from my hand."

18They called out with a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them, so that they might take the city.

19They spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.

The Deliverance

20Then Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, prayed about this and cried out to heaven.

21The LORD sent a messenger, who cut off every mighty man of valor, leader and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned in shame to his own land. When he had gone into the house of his god, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.

22So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and guided them on every side.

23Many brought offerings to the LORD in Jerusalem and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah, so that from then on he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations.

Hezekiah's Sickness and Pride

24In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. He prayed to the LORD, and the LORD spoke to him and gave him a sign.

25But Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was lifted up. So wrath came on him and on Judah and Jerusalem.

26Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD did not come on them in the days of Hezekiah.

27Hezekiah had very great riches and honor. He made himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields and all kinds of costly vessels,

28storehouses for the produce of grain, new wine and oil, and stalls for all kinds of cattle, and folds for the flocks.

29He also made cities for himself, and had flocks and herds in abundance, for God had given him very great possessions.

30This same Hezekiah stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them down to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

31So too in the matter of the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who had been sent to him to inquire about the sign that had been done in the land, God left him, to test him, to know all that was in his heart.

32The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his deeds of loyal love are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

33Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of the sons of David. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honor at his death. Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–23 and 2 Kings 18:13–19:37 — the same invasion, told in a third of the space. Chronicles leaves out Hezekiah's payment of tribute (2 Kings 18:14–16) and gives the defense of the city (vv2–8) instead.

  • v1 "After these things and this faithfulness" — ve-ha-emet, the word just said of Hezekiah, good and right and true (31:20). The invasion follows the faithfulness; it is not its punishment.

  • vv3–4, 30 "to stop the water of the springs… stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon" — Kings: how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city (2 Kings 20:20).

  • vv7–8 "there is more with us than with him. With him is an arm of flesh" — Elisha's word to his servant, those who are with us are more than those who are with them (2 Kings 6:16). Zeroa basar, an arm of flesh: Jeremiah curses the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm (Jeremiah 17:5). The people relied, va-yissamkhu, leaned on, the words of their king.

  • v12 "You shall bow down before one altar" — the Assyrian's argument in Kings (2 Kings 18:22): he takes the reform for an insult to the LORD.

  • v18 "in the language of Judah" — Yehudit, the language the king's men asked the Assyrians not to use in the hearing of the people who are on the wall (2 Kings 18:26).

  • v21 "The LORD sent a messenger, who cut off every mighty man… some of his own offspring struck him down" — Kings gives the number, a hundred and eighty-five thousand, and the names of the sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer (2 Kings 19:35, 37). Mi-tsi'ei me'av, those who came out of his own body: the god who could not save the nations did not save the king in his own house.

  • vv24–26 "his heart was lifted up… Hezekiah humbled himself" — gavah libbo, the pride of Uzziah (26:16), and va-yikkana, the humbling of 7:14. Kings tells the sickness and the sign of the shadow at length (2 Kings 20:1–11).

  • v31 "God left him, to test him, to know all that was in his heart" — the words of the wilderness, to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart (Deuteronomy 8:2). Kings tells of the envoys and Isaiah's word that all would be carried to Babylon (2 Kings 20:12–19); Chronicles names only the test.

  • v32 "his deeds of loyal love" — chasadav, the plural of chesed, said of Hezekiah, and of Josiah (35:26).

chapters.title: Manasseh's Captivity and Return
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 33

Manasseh King of Judah

1Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

2He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.

3He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had torn down. He set up altars for the Baals and made Asherahs, and he bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.

4He built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem shall My name be forever."

5He built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

6He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, practiced soothsaying, read omens and practiced sorcery, and appointed those who deal with ghosts and spirits. He did much evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

7He set the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.

8I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land that I appointed for your fathers, if only they will be careful to do all that I have commanded them, all the instruction, the statutes and the rules given through Moses."

9So Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the sons of Israel.

Captivity and Return

10The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.

11So the LORD brought on them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze shackles and took him to Babylon.

12In his distress he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.

13He prayed to Him, and God let Himself be pleaded with by him, heard his plea and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD, He is God.

14After this he built an outer wall for the City of David, west of Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance at the Fish Gate, and carried it around the Ophel and raised it very high. He put commanders of the army in all the fortified cities of Judah.

15He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the city.

16He built the altar of the LORD and sacrificed on it peace offerings and thank offerings, and he told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.

17The people still sacrificed at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

18The rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are in the records of the kings of Israel.

19His prayer, and how God let Himself be pleaded with by him, all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the sites on which he built high places and set up the Asherim and the carved images before he humbled himself, are written in the records of Hozai.

20Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in his house, and Amon his son reigned in his place.

Amon King of Judah

21Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.

22He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done. Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made, and served them.

23He did not humble himself before the LORD, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; this Amon only added to his guilt.

24His servants conspired against him and put him to death in his house.

25But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–20 and 2 Kings 21:1–18 — Kings tells Manasseh's reign as the evil that sealed the fall of Jerusalem (2 Kings 21:10–15; 23:26). Chronicles keeps the list of his sins and adds what Kings does not have: the captivity, the prayer, the return and the reform (vv10–17).

  • v7 "the carved image of the idol" — pesel ha-semel. Kings has the carved image of Asherah (2 Kings 21:7). Semel is a figure or statue: the law forbids a carved image in the form of any figure (Deuteronomy 4:16), and Ezekiel sees the image of jealousy at the gate of this house (Ezekiel 8:3, 5).

  • v11 "captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze shackles and took him to Babylon" — ba-chochim, the word of the LORD's threat to Sennacherib, I will put My hook in your nose (2 Kings 19:28). Va-ya'asruhu ba-nechushtayim… Bavelah are the words of the end of the last king, Zedekiah: they bound him with bronze shackles and brought him to Babylon (2 Kings 25:7). The worst king of Judah goes the way the kingdom will go, and comes back.

  • v12 "he sought the favor of the LORD" — chillah et penei YHWH, softened the face of the LORD, the words of Moses after the golden calf (Exodus 32:11).

  • vv13, 19 "God let Himself be pleaded with by him" — va-ye'ater lo, the rare verb of Isaac's prayer: The LORD let Himself be pleaded with (Genesis 25:21). The LORD, He is God is the cry of the people on Carmel (1 Kings 18:39).

  • v19 "the records of Hozai" — divrei Chozai. The word differs by one letter from ha-chozim, the seers, in v18, and the Greek has of the seers in both verses. As written, it is a name, otherwise unknown.

  • v20 "they buried him in his house" — Kings has in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza (2 Kings 21:18); the Greek of Chronicles also has in the garden of his house.

  • v23 "He did not humble himself… as Manasseh his father had humbled himself" — nikhna, the word of the promise at the dedication, if My people humble themselves (7:14). Father and son are measured by it.

chapters.title: Josiah and the Book of the Instruction
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 34

Josiah King of Judah

1Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.

2He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

The Land Cleansed

3In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his father, and in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images.

4They tore down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and he cut down the incense altars that stood above them. He broke the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images, crushed them to dust and scattered it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.

5He burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

6In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,

7he tore down the altars, beat the Asherim and the carved images into dust, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

The Repair of the House

8In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.

9They came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the remnant of Israel and from all Judah and Benjamin, and they returned to Jerusalem.

10They gave it into the hands of those who did the work, who were appointed over the house of the LORD, and they gave it to the workers who were working in the house of the LORD to restore and repair the house.

11They gave it to the carpenters and the builders to buy quarried stone, and timber for the couplings and for the beams of the buildings that the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.

12The men did the work faithfully. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah the Levites, of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to direct it. The Levites, all who were skilled with instruments of song,

13were over the burden bearers and directed all who did the work in every kind of service, and some of the Levites were scribes, officers and gatekeepers.

The Book Found

14While they were bringing out the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the instruction of the LORD given through Moses.

15Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.

16Shaphan brought the book to the king, and he also brought back word to the king, saying, "All that was given into the hands of your servants, they are doing.

17They have poured out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and have given it into the hands of those appointed and of those who do the work."

18Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." Shaphan read from it before the king.

19And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the instruction, that he tore his clothes.

20The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,

21"Go, inquire of the LORD for me, and for those who are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found. For great is the wrath of the LORD that is poured out on us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the LORD, to do according to all that is written in this book."

Huldah the Prophetess

22So Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke to her accordingly.

23She said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,

24Thus says the LORD: I am about to bring evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the curses that are written in the book that they have read before the king of Judah.

25Because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, to provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands, My wrath will be poured out on this place, and it will not be quenched.'

26But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, say this to him: 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: As for the words that you have heard,

27because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words against this place and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before Me and tore your clothes and wept before Me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.

28I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the evil that I will bring on this place and on its inhabitants.'" They brought back word to the king.

The Covenant Renewed

29Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

  • v5 "He burned the bones of the priests on their altars" — the word of the man of God against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel: A son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name, and on you he shall sacrifice the priests of the high places… and human bones shall be burned on you (1 Kings 13:2). speech.text: 2 Chronicles 34
Josiah King of Judah
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
The Land Cleansed

In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his father, and in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images.

They tore down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and he cut down the incense altars that stood above them. He broke the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images, crushed them to dust and scattered it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,
he tore down the altars, beat the Asherim and the carved images into dust, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
The Repair of the House

In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the remnant of Israel and from all Judah and Benjamin, and they returned to Jerusalem.

They gave it into the hands of those who did the work, who were appointed over the house of the LORD, and they gave it to the workers who were working in the house of the LORD to restore and repair the house.
They gave it to the carpenters and the builders to buy quarried stone, and timber for the couplings and for the beams of the buildings that the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.

The men did the work faithfully. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah the Levites, of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to direct it. The Levites, all who were skilled with instruments of song,
were over the burden bearers and directed all who did the work in every kind of service, and some of the Levites were scribes, officers and gatekeepers.

While they were bringing out the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the instruction of the LORD given through Moses.
Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan brought the book to the king, and he also brought back word to the king, saying, "All that was given into the hands of your servants, they are doing.
They have poured out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and have given it into the hands of those appointed and of those who do the work."
Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." Shaphan read from it before the king.
And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the instruction, that he tore his clothes.
The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,

"Go, inquire of the LORD for me, and for those who are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found. So Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke to her accordingly.
She said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,
Thus says the LORD: I am about to bring evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the curses that are written in the book that they have read before the king of Judah.
Because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, to provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands, My wrath will be poured out on this place, and it will not be quenched.'
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, say this to him: 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: As for the words that you have heard,

because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words against this place and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before Me and tore your clothes and wept before Me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.

I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the evil that I will bring on this place and on its inhabitants.'" They brought back word to the king.
The Covenant Renewed
Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites and all the people, both great and small. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

chapters.title: Josiah's Passover and His Death
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 35

The Passover

1Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.

2He set the priests at their posts and encouraged them in the service of the house of the LORD.

3He said to the Levites who taught all Israel and who were holy to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. You no longer have to carry it on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel.

4Prepare yourselves by your fathers' houses in your divisions, as David king of Israel wrote and as Solomon his son wrote.

5Stand in the holy place by the sections of the fathers' houses of your brothers, the lay people, so that each has a portion of a Levite family.

6Slaughter the Passover lamb, consecrate yourselves, and prepare it for your brothers, to do according to the word of the LORD given through Moses."

7Josiah contributed to the lay people, for all who were present, flocks of lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings, thirty thousand in number, and three thousand bulls; these were from the king's possessions.

8His officials contributed freely to the people, to the priests and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the chief officers of the house of God, gave the priests two thousand six hundred Passover offerings and three hundred bulls.

9Conaniah, with Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, the chiefs of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand Passover offerings and five hundred bulls.

10So the service was prepared, and the priests stood at their posts and the Levites by their divisions, as the king had commanded.

11They slaughtered the Passover lamb, and the priests dashed the blood they received from them while the Levites flayed the animals.

12They set apart the burnt offerings to give them to the sections of the fathers' houses of the lay people, to offer to the LORD, as it is written in the book of Moses; and so with the bulls.

13They cooked the Passover lamb with fire according to the rule, and they boiled the holy offerings in pots, in cauldrons and in pans, and carried them quickly to all the lay people.

14Afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

15The singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their posts according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer, and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to leave their service, because their brothers the Levites prepared for them.

16So all the service of the LORD was prepared that day, to keep the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, as King Josiah had commanded.

17The sons of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days.

18No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of the kings of Israel had kept such a Passover as Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

19In the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign this Passover was kept.

The Death of Josiah

20After all this, when Josiah had set the house in order, Neco king of Egypt came up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.

21But Neco sent messengers to him, saying, "What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, so that He does not destroy you."

22But Josiah would not turn his face away from him. He disguised himself to fight him, and did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and came to fight in the plain of Megiddo.

23The archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."

24So his servants took him out of the chariot and put him in his second chariot and brought him to Jerusalem, and he died. He was buried in the tombs of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

25Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the singing men and singing women have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them a statute in Israel; they are written in the Laments.

26The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his deeds of loyal love according to what is written in the instruction of the LORD,

27and his acts, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

Notes

  • vv1–19 and 2 Kings 23:21–23 — Kings gives Josiah's Passover three verses; Chronicles gives it nineteen, set out like Hezekiah's (30:1–27), with the Levites doing the work.

  • v3 "Put the holy ark in the house… You no longer have to carry it on your shoulders" — the last time the ark is named in Kings or Chronicles. The verse does not say why it was out of the house. Carrying it on the shoulders was the Levites' charge in the wilderness (Numbers 7:9; 1 Chronicles 15:15); with the ark at rest, Josiah gives them a new one, the service of the people. In the same reign Jeremiah says a day is coming when they will no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of the LORD"… nor will it be made again (Jeremiah 3:16).

  • v13 "They cooked the Passover lamb with fire according to the rule" — va-yevashlu… ba-esh. Bashal is the verb of Deuteronomy, You shall cook it and eat it in the place that the LORD your God will choose (Deuteronomy 16:7); with fire is the rule of Exodus, not… boiled at all in water, but roasted with fire (Exodus 12:9). The verse joins the two laws: the lamb over the fire, and the holy offerings boiled in pots.

  • v18 "since the days of Samuel the prophet" — Kings has since the days of the judges who judged Israel (2 Kings 23:22). Samuel was the last of them.

  • v21 "God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me" — words of a Pharaoh, and v22 calls them the words of Neco from the mouth of God. The book that says the LORD stirred the spirit of the Philistines and Arabs against Jehoram (21:16), and will say He stirred the spirit of Cyrus (36:22), here gives His word to the king of Egypt, and Josiah does not hear it.

  • vv22–23 "He disguised himself… I am badly wounded" — hitchappes, the word of Ahab at Ramoth-gilead, I will disguise myself and go into battle, and Ahab's words when the arrow struck him, for I am wounded (18:29, 33). The good king dies the way the king of Israel died.

  • v25 "they are written in the Laments" — al ha-qinot, a collection of laments for the dead. Josiah is not named in the book of Lamentations.

  • v26 "his deeds of loyal love" — chasadav, the plural of chesed, said of Hezekiah in the same words (32:32).

chapters.title: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Decree of Cyrus
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 36

Jehoahaz

1The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.

2Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.

3The king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem and laid on the land a fine of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

Jehoiakim

4The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt.

5Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.

6Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.

7Nebuchadnezzar also brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his temple in Babylon.

8The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things he did, and what was found against him, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

Jehoiachin

9Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

10At the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD, and made Zedekiah his kinsman king over Judah and Jerusalem.

Zedekiah and the Fall of Jerusalem

11Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

12He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.

13He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to the LORD, the God of Israel.

14All the chiefs of the priests and the people also broke faith more and more, according to all the detestable practices of the nations, and they defiled the house of the LORD that He had consecrated in Jerusalem.

15The LORD, the God of their fathers, sent to them by His messengers, sending again and again, because He had compassion on His people and on His dwelling place.

16But they kept mocking the messengers of God, despising His words and scoffing at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD rose against His people, until there was no remedy.

17So He brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or young woman, the old or the gray-haired. He gave them all into his hand.

18All the vessels of the house of God, great and small, the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king and of his officials, he brought them all to Babylon.

19They burned the house of God, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all its palaces with fire and destroyed all its precious things.

20He carried into exile to Babylon those who had escaped the sword, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to reign,

21to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had been paid its sabbaths. All the days that it lay waste it kept sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.

The Decree of Cyrus

22In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,

23"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has appointed me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever is among you of all His people, may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up."

Notes

  • vv1–10 and 2 Kings 23:30–24:17 — four kings in ten verses. Chronicles gives none of the mothers' names, and none of the reigns a story: each king does evil, and each is carried off, to Egypt or to Babylon.

  • v6 "bound him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon" — the words used of Manasseh (33:11) and of Zedekiah (2 Kings 25:7). Kings does not say Jehoiakim was taken; it says he lay down with his fathers (2 Kings 24:6).

  • v9 "eight years old" — the Greek of Chronicles also has eight. Kings has eighteen (2 Kings 24:8), and Kings names the king's wives among those taken with him (24:15).

  • v10 "Zedekiah his kinsman" — achiv, his brother, a word also used of a nearer or wider relative, as of Abram's nephew Lot (Genesis 14:14). Kings has his uncle, dodo (2 Kings 24:17), and so does the Greek here: his father's brother.

  • v13 "who had made him swear by God" — Ezekiel tells of the oath and its breaking: he took one of the royal offspring and made a covenant with him, and brought him under an oath (Ezekiel 17:13); shall he break the covenant and escape? (17:15).

  • v15 "sending again and again" — hashkem ve-shaloach, rising early and sending, Jeremiah's phrase: I have sent you all My servants the prophets, rising early and sending them (Jeremiah 7:25).

  • v16 "until there was no remedy" — ad le-ein marpe, from rapha, the word of the promise at the dedication, I will heal their land (7:14), and of Hezekiah's Passover, the LORD… healed the people (30:20).

  • v21 "until the land had been paid its sabbaths. All the days that it lay waste it kept sabbath" — the words of the law: Then the land will be paid its sabbaths, all the days it lies waste (Leviticus 26:34). The seventy years are Jeremiah's (Jeremiah 25:11; 29:10).

  • vv22–23 "let him go up" — ve-ya'al, the last word of the book. The decree is given again at the opening of Ezra (Ezra 1:1–3), where the sentence goes on: to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD. Chronicles ends with the exiles told to go up.
